-122.40600,37.80540.name: Pacific Fertility Center
-122.40600,37.80540.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Isabelle Ryan, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

114.25145,22.25706.name: No.18 Gaohu Road, high-tech industrial park, Conghua economic development zone, Guangzhou, Guangdong, China;510990 GUANGZHOU, GUANGDONG, P.R. CHINA Te
114.25145,22.25706.company: Guangdong Lewwin Pharmaceutical Research Institute Co., Ltd.
114.25145,22.25706.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Guangdong Lewwin Pharmaceutical Research Institute Co., Ltd.. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-117.64730,49.30722.name: Selkirk College
-117.64730,49.30722.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, September 2025
-117.64730,49.30722.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, September 2025. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-73.41600,41.35600.name: Cooper Surgical — fertility
-73.41600,41.35600.desc: Supplies much of the equipment and culture media that IVF laboratories run on, and recalled culture media in 2024 after embryos failed to develop, with lawsuits following from families whose cycles were lost. A supplier failure in this facet destroys something irreplaceable, and the regulatory framework treats the media as a device rather than as the environment an embryo develops in.

135.76800,35.01200.name: Sanatech Seed
135.76800,35.01200.desc: Sells a gene-edited tomato with raised GABA content directly to Japanese consumers, the first edited food marketed to the public anywhere. Japan classed it outside the GMO rules because no foreign DNA was inserted, so it required notification rather than approval. The product itself is unremarkable; what it established is that a country can move an edited food to market through a notification form.

11.58200,48.13400.name: European Patent Office — opposition register
11.58200,48.13400.desc: The EPO allows anyone to oppose a granted patent within nine months, and the whole file is public. Opposition has been used repeatedly against patents on conventionally bred plants, and it is the only route by which a member of the public can attack a European patent directly.

31.03350,-17.82520.name: Seed Co Group
31.03350,-17.82520.state: Harare — international headquarters in South Africa
31.03350,-17.82520.desc: Africa's largest home-grown seed company, founded in 1940 as the Seed Maize Association of Zimbabwe by farmers wanting reliable maize seed, now operating across roughly twenty African countries with maize, soya, wheat, sorghum, groundnuts, cotton, rice and vegetables, and running the largest single out-grower scheme in the seed business. Limagrain — the largest seed and plant breeding company in the European Union — bought in from 2014 and holds around 30 per cent, and the vegetable seed line is distributed with a Limagrain business unit. It also sold 49 per cent of Africa's only cottonseed company to an Indian firm part-owned by Monsanto. A farmer cooperative that became a continental company and then a partly foreign-owned one is the whole trajectory of this facet in a single organisation.

31.03350,-17.82520.name: Quton Seed Company
31.03350,-17.82520.desc: Described at the time of its sale as Africa's only cottonseed company, and notable for producing open-pollinated varieties as well as hybrids — seed a farmer can save and replant. In 2014 a 49 per cent stake was sold to an Indian seed company that is part-owned by Monsanto and holds a joint venture to sub-license engineered cotton traits across India. The detail that matters is the difference in what each side breeds: the buyer specialises in hybrid cotton, which must be repurchased every season. Whether open-pollinated lines survive a change of ownership is a question this map can only answer by recording who owns them.
